cues: Keep your hips level with your shoulders.
The lower the surface, the harder it gets.
exercises.name: Incline push-up
steps: Place your hands on a bench or sturdy ledge, a little wider than your shoulders.
Step your feet back until your body is one straight line from head to heels.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest to the edge.
Press back up until your arms are straight.

cues: Do not let your hips sag or pike up.
Elbows point back about 45 degrees, not out to the sides.
exercises.name: Push-up
steps: Start face down on the floor with your hands just wider than your shoulders and your arms straight.
Keep your body in one straight line from head to heels.
Lower yourself until your chest almost touches the floor.
Press back up to straight arms, squeezing your chest at the top.

cues: Keep your core tight so your hips do not sag.
A higher box shifts more work to your shoulders.
exercises.name: Decline push-up
steps: Place your feet on a bench or box and your hands on the floor, a little wider than your shoulders.
Hold your body in one straight line from head to heels.
Lower yourself until your chest almost touches the floor.
Press back up to straight arms.

cues: Avoid swinging or jerking.
A thicker band gives more help.
exercises.name: Band-assisted pull-up
steps: Loop a resistance band around the pull-up bar and put one bent knee in the loop.
Hold the bar with a grip a little wider than your shoulders and hang with straight arms.
Pull your elbows down toward your sides until your chin is over the bar.
Pause, then lower yourself back to straight arms.

cues: Do not drop; control the whole way down.
Stop the set when you can no longer lower slowly.
exercises.name: Negative pull-up
steps: Use a box or a jump to start with your chin over the bar and your hands a little wider than your shoulders.
Hold the top position for a moment with your chest up.
Lower yourself as slowly as you can, aiming for 3 to 5 seconds.
Hang with straight arms, then step down and reset.

cues: Start each rep from a full hang.
Keep your body still; no kicking or swinging.
exercises.name: Pull-up
steps: Hold the bar with your palms facing away, a little wider than your shoulders, and hang with straight arms.
Lean back slightly and push your chest out.
Pull your elbows down and back until the bar is near your upper chest.
Pause, then lower yourself slowly to straight arms.

cues: Think about pulling the elbows down to your ribs.
Do not swing or kick.
exercises.name: Chin-up
steps: Hold the bar with your palms facing you, hands about shoulder width apart, and hang with straight arms.
Keep your torso straight and your chest up.
Pull until your chin is over the bar, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Pause, then lower yourself slowly to straight arms.

cues: Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Walk your feet closer to make it easier.
exercises.name: Inverted row
steps: Set a bar in a rack at about waist height and lie underneath it.
Grab the bar a little wider than your shoulders and hang with straight arms and your heels on the floor.
Keep your body straight and pull your chest to the bar.
Pause, then lower yourself to straight arms.

cues: Breathe steadily.
Stop before your grip fails so you can step down safely.
exercises.name: Dead hang
steps: Hold a pull-up bar with your palms facing away, hands about shoulder width apart.
Step off so you hang with straight arms and your feet off the floor.
Keep a firm grip and let your shoulders stay slightly active, not shrugged to your ears.
Hang for the planned time, then step down.

cues: Keep your elbows pointing back, not out.
Bend your knees to make it easier.
exercises.name: Bench dip
steps: Sit on the edge of a bench and put your hands beside your hips, then slide your hips off the edge.
Straighten your arms with your legs out in front of you.
Bend your elbows to about 90 degrees, keeping your back close to the bench.
Press back up until your arms are straight.

cues: Do not swing your legs.
Stop if your shoulders pinch at the bottom.
exercises.name: Dip
steps: Grip two parallel bars and lift yourself to straight arms.
Lean slightly forward and keep your chest up.
Bend your elbows and lower until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Press back up to straight arms.

cues: Keep your heels on the floor.
Push your knees out, not in.
exercises.name: Air squat
steps: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and your toes slightly out.
Sit your hips back and bend your knees, keeping your chest and head up.
Lower as far as you can with your heels down, with your knees tracking over your toes.
Drive through your whole foot to stand back up.

cues: Your front knee stays over your foot.
Keep your feet in the same place for the whole set.
exercises.name: Split squat
steps: Stand with one foot a long step in front of the other, with your feet hip width apart.
Keep your torso upright and lower your back knee toward the floor.
Stop just above the floor with your front heel down.
Press through the front foot to stand up; finish all reps, then switch legs.

cues: Your front knee stays over your foot.
Find your step length in the first rep and keep it.
exercises.name: Bulgarian split squat
steps: Stand a long step in front of a bench and rest the top of one back foot on it.
Keep your torso upright with most of your weight on the front foot.
Lower your back knee toward the floor until your front thigh is about parallel.
Press through the front heel to stand; finish all reps, then switch legs.

cues: Take a long enough step that your front shin stays upright.
Do not let your front knee collapse inward.
exercises.name: Lunge
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart and your hands on your hips.
Step forward and lower your hips until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Keep your front knee over your foot and your torso upright.
Push through the front heel to return to standing, then repeat on the other leg.

cues: Let the working leg do the lifting, not the push-off foot.
Holding dumbbells is optional.
exercises.name: Step-up
steps: Stand facing a sturdy bench or step that puts your thigh about parallel when your foot is on it.
Place one foot fully on the step.
Push through that heel to stand up on the step.
Step back down with control; finish all reps, then switch legs.

cues: Keep your ribs down; do not arch your lower back.
Push through your heels.
exercises.name: Glute bridge
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat, about hip width apart.
Push through your heels and lift your hips until your body is in a line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes and hold for a second at the top.
Lower slowly to the floor.

cues: Keep your hips level, not tilted to one side.
Squeeze your glute at the top.
exercises.name: Single-leg glute bridge
steps: Lie on your back with your feet flat and your knees bent.
Lift one leg and pull that knee toward your chest.
Push through the heel of the other foot to lift your hips as high as you can.
Lower slowly; finish all reps, then switch legs.

cues: Hinge at the hips; do not round your back.
Keep your knees softly bent and still.
exercises.name: Good morning
steps: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart, knees slightly bent, and your hands behind your head.
Push your hips back and lean your chest forward with a flat back.
Stop when your torso is near parallel to the floor or you feel your hamstrings stretch.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.

cues: Keep your knees straight but not locked.
Use a wall for balance if you need it.
exercises.name: Calf raise
steps: Stand with the balls of your feet on the floor or the edge of a step, with your feet hip width apart.
Rise up as high as you can on your toes.
Pause for a second at the top.
Lower slowly until your heels are level or just below the step.

cues: Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs.
Do not let your hips sag or rise.
exercises.name: Plank
steps: Lie face down and prop yourself on your forearms, with your elbows right under your shoulders.
Lift your hips and rest on your toes.
Hold your body in one straight line from head to heels.
Hold for the planned time, breathing steadily.

cues: Keep your hips high and your neck in line with your spine.
Bend your bottom knee to make it easier.
exercises.name: Side plank
steps: Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder and your legs stacked.
Lift your hips off the floor so your body is a straight line from head to feet.
Hold for the planned time, then switch sides.

cues: Keep your lower back flat on the floor.
Bend your knees or bring your arms to your sides to make it easier.
exercises.name: Hollow hold
steps: Lie on your back with your arms overhead and your legs straight.
Press your lower back into the floor.
Lift your shoulders and your straight legs a few inches off the floor.
Hold the shape for the planned time.

cues: Keep your core tight in the push-up position.
Step instead of jumping to make it easier.
exercises.name: Burpee
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart.
Squat down and place your hands on the floor, then jump or step your feet back to a push-up position.
Lower your chest to the floor, then press up.
Jump or step your feet back under your hips and jump up with your arms overhead.

cues: Use your elbows to push your knees out at the bottom.
Keep your heels on the floor.
exercises.name: Goblet squat
steps: Hold a dumbbell upright against your chest with both hands, elbows pointing down.
Stand with your feet a little wider than your shoulders and your toes slightly out.
Squat down between your legs, keeping your chest and head up.
Pause at the bottom, then stand back up.

cues: Keep the weights close to your legs.
Hinge at the hips; your knees stay softly bent and still.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and stand with your feet about shoulder width apart.
Soften your knees and push your hips back as you lower the weights along your legs.
Stop when you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, with your back flat.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.

cues: Lower for about twice as long as you lift.
Keep your wrists straight over your elbows.
exercises.name: Dumbbell bench press
steps: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand at the sides of your chest, palms facing forward.
Plant your feet on the floor and keep your shoulder blades pinched together.
Press the weights straight up until your arms are straight.
Lower slowly until your elbows are about 90 degrees.

cues: Keep your torso still; the back does the work, not the arm.
Do not twist as you pull.
exercises.name: Dumbbell row
steps: Place one knee and the same-side hand on a bench, with your back flat and a dumbbell in your other hand.
Let the dumbbell hang at arm's length.
Pull it up to the side of your chest, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Lower slowly; finish all reps, then switch sides.

cues: Do not lean back or use your legs.
Keep your ribs down.
exercises.name: Dumbbell overhead press
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms forward.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Press the dumbbells straight up until your arms are straight.
Lower slowly back to your shoulders.

cues: Use a light weight and do not swing.
Lead with your elbows, as if pouring water from a jug.
exercises.name: Lateral raise
steps: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they are about parallel to the floor.
Pause for a second.
Lower slowly to your sides.

cues: Keep your upper arms still.
Do not swing your body to lift the weight.
exercises.name: Biceps curl
steps: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing forward.
Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
Curl the weights up toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.

cues: Only your forearms move.
Brace your core so you do not arch your back.
exercises.name: Triceps extension
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart, holding one dumbbell with both hands overhead and your arms straight.
Keep your upper arms close to your head with your elbows pointing forward.
Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Straighten your arms to lift it back up.

cues: Keep your chest up and your back flat.
Use a rack with safety bars set below your lowest point.
exercises.name: Barbell back squat
steps: Set the bar on a rack at just below shoulder height and step under it, with the bar across your upper back.
Lift it off the rack, step back, and set your feet about shoulder width apart.
Bend your hips and knees to lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Drive through your whole foot to stand back up.

cues: Keep your back flat; do not round it.
Brace your core before each rep.
exercises.name: Barbell deadlift
steps: Stand with your feet hip width apart and the bar over your mid-foot.
Bend down and grip the bar just outside your legs, with your back flat and your chest up.
Push the floor away and stand up with the bar close to your legs.
Lower the bar along the same path, then reset.

cues: Keep your shoulder blades pinched and your feet planted.
Use safety bars or a spotter.
exercises.name: Barbell bench press
steps: Lie on a flat bench with your eyes under the bar and your feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar a little wider than your shoulders and unrack it over your chest.
Lower the bar to your mid-chest with control.
Press it back up until your arms are straight.

cues: Move your head back, then through, as the bar passes.
Do not lean back.
exercises.name: Barbell overhead press
steps: Set the bar at chest height on a rack and grip it just wider than your shoulders.
Lift it off, step back, and hold it at your collarbone with your elbows slightly forward.
Squeeze your glutes and press the bar straight up until your arms are straight.
Lower it back to your collarbone with control.

cues: Start with a bigger edge and stay within your plan.
Stop at any sharp finger pain.
exercises.name: Hangboard hang
steps: Hold a large hangboard edge with an open hand or half crimp, fingers on the edge.
Step off the floor with your feet clear of the ground and your arms nearly straight.
Keep your shoulders engaged, not shrugged.
Hang for the planned time, then step down.

cues: Push the floor away so your shoulder blades spread.
Keep the stretch gentle, never sharp.
exercises.name: Cat stretch
steps: Get on your hands and knees, hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Tuck your chin and let your head drop.
Pull your belly in and round your whole back toward the ceiling.
Hold, breathing slowly, then relax.

cues: If your knees complain, skip this one or put a folded towel behind them.
Let your shoulders sink away from your ears.
exercises.name: Child's pose
steps: Start on your hands and knees and walk your hands forward.
Sit your hips back toward your heels.
Rest your forehead on the floor and let your arms lie relaxed.
Breathe into your back and hold.

cues: Squeeze the glute of the back leg.
Do not arch your lower back.
exercises.name: Kneeling hip flexor stretch
steps: Kneel on a mat, then step one foot forward so that knee is bent at about 90 degrees.
Keep your back knee on the floor and your torso upright.
Tuck your tailbone under and shift your weight forward until you feel the front of your back hip stretch.
Hold, then switch sides.

cues: Hinge at the hips and keep your back long, not rounded.
Reach only as far as is comfortable.
exercises.name: Seated hamstring stretch
steps: Sit on the floor with one leg straight in front of you.
Bend the other knee and rest that foot against your inner thigh.
Lean forward from your hips and reach toward your ankle.
Stop when you feel a stretch behind the straight knee, then hold and switch sides.

cues: Keep the top foot flexed to protect the knee.
Pull only until you feel the stretch in the outer hip.
exercises.name: Figure-four stretch
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet on the floor.
Rest one ankle on the opposite knee.
Reach through and hold the bottom thigh, then pull both legs gently toward your chest.
Keep your head and shoulders relaxed, hold, then switch sides.

cues: The knee does not need to reach the floor.
Keep both shoulders on the floor.
exercises.name: Knee across the body
steps: Lie on your back with one leg straight and the other knee bent.
Guide the bent knee across your body with the opposite hand.
Open your other arm out to the side and turn your head the other way.
Hold, breathing slowly, then switch sides.

cues: Hold under the knee, not on the kneecap.
Keep your lower back resting on the floor.
exercises.name: One knee to chest
steps: Lie on your back with your legs straight.
Bring one knee up and hold it just below the kneecap.
Gently pull the knee toward your chest and your nose.
Keep the other leg relaxed on the floor, hold, then switch sides.

cues: Keep your knees close together.
Do not twist your lower back.
exercises.name: Side-lying quad stretch
steps: Lie on your side with your bottom knee bent for balance and your head on your arm.
Bend your top knee and hold that foot with your top hand.
Press your hip forward as you gently pull your heel toward your glute.
Hold, then roll over and switch sides.

cues: Keep your heel down and toes pointing forward.
Keep your head, hips and back heel in one line.
exercises.name: Wall calf stretch
steps: Stand facing a wall and place your hands on it at chest height.
Step one foot back, with your front knee bent.
Press the back heel into the floor and lean toward the wall.
Keep your back leg straight, hold, then switch sides.

cues: Turn from your ribs, not by swinging your arms.
Keep your knees soft.
exercises.name: Standing trunk twist
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and your hands on your hips.
Keep your hips facing forward.
Slowly turn your upper body to one side until you feel a stretch.
Hold, return to the middle, then turn to the other side.

cues: Keep your shoulder down, not shrugged.
Pull on the arm, not the elbow joint.
exercises.name: Cross-body shoulder stretch
steps: Stand tall and bring one arm straight across your chest.
Hold that arm just above the elbow with your other hand.
Gently pull it toward your chest until you feel the back of your shoulder stretch.
Hold, then switch arms.

cues: Keep your ribs down and do not arch your back.
Stop at a comfortable stretch.
exercises.name: Triceps stretch
steps: Stand tall and raise one arm, then bend the elbow so your hand reaches down your back.
Hold that elbow with your other hand.
Gently pull the elbow back and toward the other side.
Hold, then switch arms.

cues: Spread your toes and press evenly through all four corners of each foot.
Keep your knees soft, not locked.
exercises.name: Mountain

cautions: Poor balance can make this unsafe; keep a wall or chair within reach (NCCIH lists balance issues among reasons to modify poses).
pose.effect: Builds standing posture and body awareness; lightly works the legs and core.
pose.holdNote: Hold about 30 seconds, around 5 slow breaths.

steps: Stand with your feet hip width apart and your weight even across both feet.
Let your arms hang by your sides with your palms facing forward.
Lengthen the crown of your head toward the ceiling and relax your shoulders away from your ears.
Breathe slowly and hold.

cues: Keep your knees over your ankles, not past your toes.
Let your weight sit in your heels.
exercises.name: Chair

cautions: With a knee or other preexisting injury, shorten the range or skip it (NCCIH lists preexisting injuries among reasons to modify poses).
Poor balance can make this unsafe; keep a wall or chair within reach (NCCIH lists balance issues among reasons to modify poses).
pose.effect: Strengthens the thighs, glutes and back.
pose.holdNote: Hold 15 to 30 seconds; sit higher if your thighs burn before then.

steps: Stand with your feet hip width apart.
Bend your knees and sit your hips back as if lowering into a chair.
Raise your arms alongside your ears.
Keep your chest lifted, hold, then press through your feet to stand.

cues: Keep the front knee in line with your second toe.
Lift your chest without arching your lower back.
exercises.name: Warrior I

cautions: With a knee or other preexisting injury, shorten the range or skip it (NCCIH lists preexisting injuries among reasons to modify poses).
Poor balance can make this unsafe; keep a wall or chair within reach (NCCIH lists balance issues among reasons to modify poses).
pose.effect: Strengthens the legs; stretches the hip flexors and chest.

steps: Step one foot back about a leg's length and turn the back foot out slightly, heel down.
Bend the front knee over the ankle.
Square your hips toward the front as far as is comfortable.
Raise both arms overhead, hold, then step together and switch sides.

cues: Stack your shoulders over your hips, not leaning toward the front leg.
Keep the front knee pointing the way your toes point.
exercises.name: Warrior II

cautions: With a knee or other preexisting injury, shorten the range or skip it (NCCIH lists preexisting injuries among reasons to modify poses).
Poor balance can make this unsafe; keep a wall or chair within reach (NCCIH lists balance issues among reasons to modify poses).
pose.effect: Strengthens the thighs and shoulders; stretches the inner thighs.

steps: Stand with your feet about a leg's length apart and turn your front foot out, back foot slightly in.
Bend the front knee over the ankle.
Stretch your arms out level with the floor and look over your front hand.
Hold, then straighten the leg and switch sides.

cues: Keep both legs straight but the knees unlocked.
Rest your hand on your shin, not on the knee joint.
exercises.name: Triangle

cautions: Poor balance can make this unsafe; keep a wall or chair within reach (NCCIH lists balance issues among reasons to modify poses).
With glaucoma or severe high blood pressure, ask your provider first, because the head sits below the heart (NCCIH lists both among reasons to modify poses).
pose.effect: Stretches the hamstrings, hips and side body.

steps: Stand with your feet about a leg's length apart, front foot turned out.
Reach your front arm forward, then tip from your hip and rest that hand on your shin or a block.
Stretch your top arm toward the ceiling.
Hold, then come up on an inhale and switch sides.

cues: Keep the front knee over the ankle.
Turn your chest toward the ceiling.
exercises.name: Extended side angle

cautions: With a knee or other preexisting injury, shorten the range or skip it (NCCIH lists preexisting injuries among reasons to modify poses).
Poor balance can make this unsafe; keep a wall or chair within reach (NCCIH lists balance issues among reasons to modify poses).
pose.effect: Strengthens the legs; stretches the side body and groin.

steps: Start in Warrior II with the front knee bent.
Lower your front forearm to your front thigh, or your hand to a block.
Reach the other arm long over your ear.
Hold, then return to Warrior II and switch sides.

cues: Fix your eyes on one still point.
Press the foot and leg into each other.
exercises.name: Tree

cautions: Poor balance can make this unsafe; keep a wall or chair within reach (NCCIH lists balance issues among reasons to modify poses).
pose.effect: Trains balance and the standing leg and hip.

steps: Stand tall and shift your weight onto one foot.
Place the other foot on your calf or inner thigh, never on the knee.
Bring your palms together at your chest, or raise them overhead.
Hold, then lower the foot and switch sides.

cues: Bend your knees rather than rounding hard.
Come up slowly to avoid light-headedness.
exercises.name: Standing forward fold

cautions: With glaucoma or severe high blood pressure, ask your provider first, because the head sits below the heart (NCCIH lists both among reasons to modify poses).
With lumbar spine disease, ask your provider first (NCCIH lists it among reasons to modify poses).
pose.effect: Stretches the hamstrings, calves and back.

steps: Stand with your feet hip width apart.
Hinge forward from your hips with a long spine and bend your knees as much as you need.
Let your head and arms hang, or hold opposite elbows.
Hold, then roll up slowly with your knees bent.

cues: Keep your front knee over the ankle.
Tuck your tailbone slightly so your lower back stays long.
exercises.name: Low lunge

cautions: With a knee or other preexisting injury, shorten the range or skip it (NCCIH lists preexisting injuries among reasons to modify poses).
Poor balance can make this unsafe; keep a wall or chair within reach (NCCIH lists balance issues among reasons to modify poses).
pose.effect: Stretches the hip flexors and thighs.

steps: From hands and knees, step one foot forward between your hands.
Lower your back knee to the floor, on a folded mat if you like.
Sink your hips forward and down, then raise your torso and arms.
Hold, then step back and switch sides.

cues: Move slowly, one breath per movement.
Press the floor away so your shoulder blades spread.
exercises.name: Cat-cow

cautions: With lumbar spine disease, ask your provider first (NCCIH lists it among reasons to modify poses).
Rest on your forearms if your wrists complain.
pose.effect: Mobilizes the spine; gently works the core.
pose.holdNote: Move for about 30 seconds, around 5 breaths each way.

steps: Start on your hands and knees with your wrists under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Inhale and let your belly drop as you lift your chest and tailbone (cow).
Exhale and round your back toward the ceiling, tucking your chin (cat).
Move between the two with your breath.

cues: Put a folded towel behind your knees if they complain.
Let your shoulders sink away from your ears.
exercises.name: Child's pose

cautions: With a knee or other preexisting injury, shorten the range or skip it (NCCIH lists preexisting injuries among reasons to modify poses).
With glaucoma or severe high blood pressure, ask your provider first, because the head sits below the heart (NCCIH lists both among reasons to modify poses).
pose.effect: Gently stretches the back, hips and thighs; a resting pose.
pose.holdNote: Hold 30 to 60 seconds; it is a resting pose, so longer is fine.

steps: Kneel and sit your hips back toward your heels, knees apart if that is more comfortable.
Fold your torso forward and rest your forehead on the floor.
Let your arms lie forward or alongside your legs.
Breathe into your back and hold.

cues: Spread your fingers and press through your whole hand.
Bend your knees to keep your back long rather than chasing straight legs.
exercises.name: Downward dog

cautions: With glaucoma or severe high blood pressure, ask your provider first, because the head sits below the heart (NCCIH lists both among reasons to modify poses).
Take weight off your wrists by pressing into your fingertips, or use child's pose instead if they hurt.
pose.effect: Stretches the hamstrings, calves and back; loads the shoulders and arms.

steps: Start on your hands and knees, hands shoulder width apart.
Tuck your toes and lift your hips up and back.
Press the floor away and lengthen your spine, bending your knees as much as you need.
Hold, then lower your knees to rest.

cues: Keep your elbows bent and close to your ribs.
Keep your neck long, looking down or slightly forward.
exercises.name: Cobra

cautions: With lumbar spine disease, ask your provider first (NCCIH lists it among reasons to modify poses).
pose.effect: Strengthens the back and stretches the front of the chest and abdomen.

steps: Lie face down with your palms under your shoulders and elbows tucked in.
Press your pubic bone and the tops of your feet into the floor.
Peel your head and chest up, using your back muscles more than your hands.
Hold, then lower down slowly.

cues: Keep your shoulders away from your ears.
Stop where you feel a gentle arch, never a pinch.
exercises.name: Sphinx

cautions: With lumbar spine disease, ask your provider first (NCCIH lists it among reasons to modify poses).
pose.effect: A gentler back extension than cobra; stretches the front of the torso.

steps: Lie face down and bring your forearms to the floor with your elbows under your shoulders.
Press your forearms down and lift your chest.
Keep your legs relaxed and your hips on the floor.
Hold, breathing slowly, then lower down.

cues: Lift only as high as stays comfortable in your lower back.
Reach your arms back and your legs long.
exercises.name: Locust

cautions: With lumbar spine disease, ask your provider first (NCCIH lists it among reasons to modify poses).
pose.effect: Strengthens the back and glutes.

steps: Lie face down with your arms by your sides and your forehead on the floor.
Lift your head, chest and arms a little off the floor, or lift your legs one at a time.
Keep your neck long.
Hold, then lower with control.

cues: Squeeze your glutes rather than arching your lower back.
Keep your neck relaxed and your gaze toward the ceiling.
exercises.name: Bridge

cautions: With lumbar spine disease, ask your provider first (NCCIH lists it among reasons to modify poses).
In pregnancy, avoid long periods lying on your back (NCCIH).
Do not turn your head while your hips are lifted.
pose.effect: Strengthens the glutes and hamstrings; stretches the front of the hips.

steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet hip width apart, close to your hips.
Press your feet down and lift your hips.
Keep your arms by your sides and your knees over your ankles.
Hold, then lower your spine down one bone at a time.

cues: Sit on a cushion until your knees are lower than your hips.
Switch which shin is in front halfway.
exercises.name: Easy pose

cautions: With a knee or other preexisting injury, shorten the range or skip it (NCCIH lists preexisting injuries among reasons to modify poses).
Never force your knees down into a deeper cross-legged or lotus position; Cramer et al. found lotus variations among the postures reported in adverse event cases.
pose.effect: A comfortable base for breathing and for the start or end of a flow.

steps: Sit on a folded blanket with your legs loosely crossed at the shins.
Rest your hands on your knees.
Lengthen your spine and relax your shoulders.
Breathe slowly.

cues: Sit on a folded blanket if your lower back rounds.
Keep your thighs gently pressing down.
exercises.name: Staff

cautions: With lumbar spine disease, ask your provider first (NCCIH lists it among reasons to modify poses).
pose.effect: Builds sitting posture; prepares for seated folds.

steps: Sit with your legs straight in front of you and your feet flexed.
Press your palms into the floor beside your hips.
Sit tall, lifting through the crown of your head.
Breathe and hold.

cues: Sit on a folded blanket to ease your hips.
Never push your knees down with your hands.
exercises.name: Butterfly

cautions: With a knee or other preexisting injury, shorten the range or skip it (NCCIH lists preexisting injuries among reasons to modify poses).
pose.effect: Stretches the inner thighs and hips.

steps: Sit tall and bring the soles of your feet together, knees falling out to the sides.
Hold your feet or ankles.
Lengthen your spine and let your knees lower on their own.
Hold, breathing slowly.

cues: Lead with your chest, not your head.
Keep a soft bend in your knees to protect your hamstrings.
exercises.name: Seated forward fold

cautions: With lumbar spine disease, ask your provider first (NCCIH lists it among reasons to modify poses).
pose.effect: Stretches the hamstrings and back.

steps: Sit with your legs straight and your knees slightly bent if needed.
Hinge forward from your hips with a long spine.
Hold your shins, ankles or feet, or loop a strap around your feet.
Hold, then roll up slowly.

cues: Lengthen your spine on each inhale and twist on each exhale.
Keep both sit bones on the floor.
exercises.name: Seated twist

cautions: With lumbar spine disease, ask your provider first (NCCIH lists it among reasons to modify poses).
With a knee or other preexisting injury, shorten the range or skip it (NCCIH lists preexisting injuries among reasons to modify poses).
pose.effect: Rotates and stretches the spine and outer hip.

steps: Sit with your legs straight, then cross one foot over the opposite thigh with the knee up.
Hug that knee with the opposite arm, or place your elbow outside it.
Press the other hand into the floor behind you and sit tall.
Turn gently from your ribs, hold, then switch sides.

cues: Keep your head and tailbone on the floor.
Hold your shins instead of your feet if your shoulders strain.
exercises.name: Happy baby

cautions: In pregnancy, avoid long periods lying on your back (NCCIH).
With a knee or other preexisting injury, shorten the range or skip it (NCCIH lists preexisting injuries among reasons to modify poses).
pose.effect: Stretches the inner thighs, hips and lower back.

steps: Lie on your back and bring your knees toward your armpits.
Hold the outsides of your feet or your shins.
Let your knees open wide and gently pull them toward the floor.
Rock slightly from side to side if it feels good.

cues: Hold under the knees rather than pulling on the kneecaps.
Rock gently side to side to massage your lower back if it feels good.
exercises.name: Knees to chest

cautions: In pregnancy, avoid long periods lying on your back (NCCIH).
With a knee or other preexisting injury, shorten the range or skip it (NCCIH lists preexisting injuries among reasons to modify poses).
pose.effect: Gently stretches the lower back and hips.

steps: Lie on your back and draw both knees toward your chest.
Hold your shins or hug your knees with both arms.
Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
Breathe slowly and hold.

cues: Put a folded blanket under your hips if it is comfortable.
Come out by bending your knees and rolling to one side.
exercises.name: Legs up the wall

cautions: With glaucoma or severe high blood pressure, ask your provider first, because the head sits below the heart (NCCIH lists both among reasons to modify poses).
In pregnancy, avoid long periods lying on your back (NCCIH).
pose.effect: A restful pose that eases tired legs.
pose.holdNote: Hold 1 to 3 minutes where time allows; the New Me flow holds it for its rest time.

steps: Sit sideways beside a wall with one hip touching it.
Swing your legs up the wall as you lower your back to the floor.
Shuffle your hips close to the wall, bending your knees if your hamstrings pull.
Rest your arms by your sides and breathe slowly.

cues: Put a pillow under your knees if your lower back is tight.
Cover up if you cool down.
exercises.name: Corpse

cautions: In pregnancy, avoid long periods lying on your back (NCCIH).
pose.effect: Rest to finish a practice.

steps: Lie on your back with your legs hip width apart and your feet falling open.
Rest your arms a little away from your sides with your palms up.
Close your eyes and let your body feel heavy.
Breathe naturally and let go of effort.
